claims.claim: Cyprian put off deciding the case of the lapsed until the bishops could meet, and the Roman clergy, without a bishop, agreed; Cyprian says Novatian wrote their letter
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 4-5 (anf05 l.33479-33499; Hartel Ep. 55)

claims.claim: Felicissimus and five presbyters broke with Cyprian, and the party took up the charge that he was too strict with the lapsed
claims.witness: Hefele I, sec. 5 (hefele_history v1 l.6316-6358), citing Cyprian's letters

claims.claim: Some of the lapsed were pressing to receive communion before any decision
Cyprian returned to Carthage after Easter 251, after an absence from February 250
claims.witness: Hefele, History of the Councils I, sec. 5 (hefele_history v1 l.6309-6366)

claims.claim: The Carthage council met in 251, probably in May; the Rome council probably in October 251
claims.witness: Hefele I, sec. 5 (l.6366-6369, 6484); McGiffert's note to Eusebius VI.43 follows Hefele

claims.claim: A large number of African bishops met, weighed Scripture on both sides, and chose a middle course: hope not denied to the lapsed, long penance, each case examined
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6 (anf05 l.33508-33524; Hartel l.7600-7616)

claims.claim: Those who took certificates were to be admitted after examination; those who sacrificed were to be helped at death
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 17 (anf05 l.33781-33783; Hartel l.7978-7980)

claims.claim: The decisions were collected in a little book, now lost
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6; Leclercq's note in Hefele-Leclercq I.1 (fra slice l.144-145)

claims.claim: Felicissimus and five presbyters were excommunicated by the African bishops
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Cornelius on Fortunatus and Felicissimus 9 (anf05 l.34755-34766); Hefele I, sec. 5 (l.6369-6372) places it at this council

claims.claim: Cornelius held a council at Rome that agreed with Carthage
claims.witness: Cyprian, Letter to Antonianus 6 (anf05 l.33525-33529; Hartel l.7614-7615)

claims.claim: Sixty bishops and many more presbyters and deacons met at Rome; Novatian and his followers were declared strangers to the church; the fallen were to be healed with the medicines of repentance
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.43.2, from Cornelius's letters (npnf201 l.38270-38299)

claims.claim: Novatian wrote to the churches that those who had sacrificed should not be admitted to the mysteries, and their pardon left to God
claims.witness: Socrates IV.28, reporting Novatian's letters (npnf202 l.14083-14090)

claims.claim: Dionysius of Alexandria wrote to Novatian that it were better to suffer everything than divide the church
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.45, quoting the letter (npnf201 l.38922-38931)

claims.claim: Fabius of Antioch seemed to lean toward Novatian's party
The next year the African bishops granted peace to all the lapsed who had kept repenting, as a new persecution drew near
claims.witness: Synodal letter of the African bishops to Cornelius 1 (anf05 l.34280-34299, ANF Ep. 53); dated 252 by Hefele I, sec. 5 (l.6505-6507)

claims.claim: Novatian's church kept its strict discipline in Phrygia and Paphlagonia in Socrates's day

contested_claims.claim: Whether a synod at Antioch on the Novatians met
contested_claims.sides: Eusebius VI.46 says Dionysius was invited to the synod at Antioch where some were trying to establish Novatian's schism; McGiffert (note to VI.46) thinks Eusebius took it to have met and that it probably did; Hefele, Dittrich and others doubt it; Hefele will not rely on the Libellus Synodicus when it stands alone

contested_claims.claim: Whether Novatus of Carthage was one of the five presbyters condemned with Felicissimus
contested_claims.sides: Hefele I, sec. 5: not known, asserted by some and denied by others; Leclercq's note, after Paul Monceaux: he was one of the five

contested_claims.claim: How many councils met in 251 on the lapsed
contested_claims.sides: Hefele I, sec. 5: two, at Carthage and Rome; he says several editors of the acts and historians, misreading the documents, made them four

absent_details.note: The Carthage book of decisions is lost (Cyprian names it; Leclercq: nothing of this council remains). No acts of the Rome council are held; Eusebius summarises Cornelius's letters, which survive only through him.

absent_details.detail: The names and number of the bishops at Carthage in 251
absent_details.note: Cyprian says only 'a large number'. The synodal letter of the next council, to Cornelius, names forty-two bishops, but it belongs to that later council.
No source of the time gives them; May and October are Hefele's reconstruction.

absent_details.detail: Novatian's own account of the councils
absent_details.note: No letter of Novatian's on the councils is held. His rule comes through Socrates, and the Roman clergy letter Cyprian says he wrote comes before the councils.
